channel.title: PixlWrk Journal
channel.description: Practical thinking on websites, digital strategy, marketing, systems and automation.

item.title: Website redesign or rebuild: how to decide what you actually need
item.description: A dated website does not automatically need replacing. Here is how to separate design problems, content problems, technical problems and structural problems before committing to a rebuild.

item.title: Small-business SEO: fix the foundations before publishing more content
item.description: SEO is not a race to publish the most articles. Strong results usually begin with technical accessibility, clear service pages, search intent and sensible internal structure.

item.title: PPC: what to fix before increasing your Google Ads budget
item.description: More ad spend can amplify a good acquisition route—or expose a weak one faster. Check targeting, tracking, landing pages and lead quality before simply raising the budget.

item.title: Social media marketing: choose the right channels instead of trying to be everywhere
item.description: A business does not need to post on every social network. Decide what role social should play, where the audience pays attention and what content the team can sustain well.

item.title: A practical digital marketing plan for a small business
item.description: A digital marketing plan does not need twenty channels and a huge deck. It needs a clear audience, proposition, acquisition route, conversion journey and measurement rhythm.

item.title: Where AI and automation actually help a small business
item.description: The best automation projects usually begin with a repetitive process and a clear hand-off—not with a tool. Here is how to spot useful AI and workflow opportunities without automating confusion.
